reasons: Data shapes are not checked when the app runs.
Most functions are not in this packet, so their error handling is unknown.
No tests exist in the packet.

terms.meaning: a library that sends web requests to the server
a written description of what a piece of data must look like
a named description of an object's fields, used in TypeScript
the checks made before the app runs
the prefix in a web address that identifies the server's feature set

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Server address and HTTP client
sections.what: Reads the server address from a setting, falls back to the local port 8000 address, and creates a shared client that adds the API path and JSON header to every request.
sections.why: Likely reason: one shared client means every call to the server is set up the same way.
sections.watch_out: If the setting is missing, the app quietly uses the local address, so a wrong production address shows up only as connection errors.

sections.name: IndexFolderRequest
sections.title: Shape of an indexing request
sections.what: Describes the data sent to start indexing: the folder path, whether to include subfolders, and the collection name.
sections.why: Likely reason: naming the fields keeps the form and the server in agreement.
sections.watch_out: This is only a compile-time description, so a server that changes its fields will not be caught here.

sections.name: IndexFolderResponse
sections.title: Shape of an indexing reply
sections.what: Describes the indexing reply: a success flag, a message, file and chunk counts, and a list of errors.
sections.why: Likely reason: the results panel depends on these exact fields.
sections.watch_out: Missing fields in the real reply are not caught here, so the results panel can break when the app runs.

sections.name: QueryRequest
sections.title: Shape of a question request
sections.what: Describes the data sent with a question: the text, how many passages to use, optional folder and file type filters, and the collection.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the question form and the server in agreement.
sections.watch_out: The passage count is optional here, so a caller that leaves it out depends on the server's default.

sections.name: Source
sections.title: Shape of one source reference
sections.what: Describes one source: file name and path, an optional SharePoint link, optional page, slide or sheet, and an optional relevance score.
sections.why: Likely reason: the source cards use these fields to show where text came from.
sections.watch_out: Optional fields may be missing, so display code must check for them before using them.

sections.name: Evidence
sections.title: Shape of one search result
sections.what: Describes the fields of one piece of evidence returned by a search, such as the text, file name, page or slide number, and rank.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives the editor a checklist of fields, so code that uses results is checked before it runs.
sections.watch_out: These checks happen only when the frontend is built. The backend can send different data and nothing stops it at run time.

sections.name: QueryResponse
sections.title: Shape of a query answer
sections.what: Describes the full reply to a question: the answer text, its sources, the evidence list, the analysis, a confidence label, and metadata.
sections.why: Mirrors the response the backend builds, so the screen knows which fields to read.
sections.watch_out: The analysis and metadata fields accept any data, so a misspelled field name is not caught.

sections.name: FolderInfo
sections.title: Shape of one folder
sections.what: Describes one SharePoint folder: its name, its address path, and when it was created and last changed.
sections.why: Matches the folder entries the backend returns.
sections.watch_out: The dates are plain text here, so a badly formatted date is not caught.

sections.name: ListFoldersResponse
sections.title: Shape of the folder list reply
sections.what: Describes the folder list reply: a success flag, the list of folders, and a count.
sections.why: Matches the reply from the folder listing route.
sections.watch_out: The count is taken from the backend as it is and is not checked against the list.

sections.name: healthCheck
sections.title: Backend health check call
sections.what: Asks the backend whether it is running and returns its health details.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the screen show whether the backend can be reached.
sections.watch_out: Likely: the paths in this file leave out the /api/v1 prefix the backend uses, so the base address set near the top of the file must include it.

sections.name: listFolders
sections.title: Get SharePoint folders call
sections.what: Asks the backend for the folders under a SharePoint path. If no path is given, it uses Shared Documents.
sections.why: Likely reason: a default path lets the screen list the main library without knowing its exact name.
sections.watch_out: The default must match the library name in the user's SharePoint site, or the request fails or returns nothing useful.

sections.name: indexFolder
sections.title: Start indexing call
sections.what: Sends a folder and its options to the backend so the documents there can be read and stored. Returns the backend's reply.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the request details in one place so screens do not build web addresses themselves.
sections.watch_out: This function sets no timeout of its own, so the caller waits as long as the connection stays open during indexing.

sections.name: query
sections.title: Ask a question call
sections.what: Sends a question with optional filters to the backend and returns the answer.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the question request format in one place.
sections.watch_out: Answers can take many seconds, and this function sets no timeout of its own, so the screen must show progress.

sections.name: listCollections
sections.title: List collections call
sections.what: Asks the backend for the list of saved document collections.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a screen show which collections exist.
sections.watch_out: The result is used as it is, so a change in the reply shape can break the screen.

sections.name: deleteCollection
sections.title: Delete collection call
sections.what: Asks the backend to delete a saved collection by its name.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the screen remove a collection that is no longer needed.
sections.watch_out: The backend deletes the collection permanently, and this function does not ask for confirmation, so the calling screen must.

summary: Holds the shared connection to the backend server and the data shapes for indexing, questions, sources and folders. Only the first part of the file is visible in this packet.
purpose: Gives the rest of the frontend one place to talk to the server and one agreed description of the data.
why: Likely reason: keeping the calls and data shapes in one file means a server change needs only one edit.
how: Reads the server address from a setting, or falls back to the local address on port 8000. Creates a shared client that adds the API path and JSON header. Declares the shapes of the requests and replies. Other named functions, which are not in this packet, wrap the calls: healthCheck, listFolders, indexFolder, query, listCollections and deleteCollection.
inputs: The NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL setting, and the data components pass in.
outputs: The shared client, the data shapes, and the functions used by components.
risks: The data shapes are checked only at compile time, so a change in the server reply can break a screen with no error here. A missing setting silently falls back to the local address.
debug: If every request fails, check the address setting and that the server runs on that address. If a screen shows missing data, compare the reply with the matching shape.
